subject: Print for sale in Website
bodyText:
Pop 1967
Watercolour

DESCRIPTION
Charlie Rogers included a bottle of Brown Ale in many of his interior and bar paintings, particularly when his father ‘Pop’ features in the same painting. It seems this was Pop’s drink of choice.
This exceptional domestic scene features a rare glimpse inside the living room of the Rogers family home during their residency at Westbourne Avenue, near Saltwell Park.
This watercolour painting is generally regarded by supporters and academics as Charlie’s finest interior painting.

A GOOD CHOICE ?
Charlie’s finest domestic  scene simply has to be introduced into your Charlie Rogers collection.

Note
Newcastle Brown Ale is perceived in the UK as a working-man's beer, with a long association with heavy industry, the traditional economic staple of the North East of England.

DIMENSIONS
TBC

PRICE
TBC

All images are for illustrative purposes only

subject: BOOK PDF. Low Res
bodyText:
Hi Tom
Regarding including details of the new book and offering it for sale on the website, we could include something similar to this which is the most recent Cornish book as advertised on their website. Our book is published by Littlecroft Publishing and is available for £25.
We could include a couple of pages from the book such as these together with the photos I have included. Check out the book pdf to reproduce pages.

Cheers
Brian

BOOK PDF. Low Res

Sent from my iPhone

product.description: Regarding including details of the new book and offering it for sale on the website, we could include something similar to this which is the most recent Cornish book as advertised on their website. Our book is published by Littlecroft Publishing and is available for £25.
product.notes: We could include a couple of pages from the book such as these together with the photos I have included. Check out the book pdf to reproduce pages.

attachments.name: image0.jpeg
attachments.visualDescription: A scan of a book page, not a painting. A flat deep wine red field with three lines of cream serif type centred slightly above the middle: the quotation "I feel like I have spent much of my career pursued by bulldozers." attributed in bold to Charlie Rogers. Landscape format, no imagery, no signature.

attachments.name: image1.jpeg
attachments.visualDescription: A scan of page 7 of the book, a three column Prologue spread headed "The recent discovery of a collection of work by Gateshead artist Charles Henry Rogers" by Brian Rankin, with a running head "CHARLIE ROGERS - PURSUED BY BULLDOZERS" in wine red. Two reproductions sit in the page: a dense, warm toned oil of the Bigg Market, Newcastle captioned "Bigg Market, Newcastle. Charlie Rogers at his finest", and a grey and buff watercolour of terraced houses held up by raking timber shores, captioned "Before the bulldozers".

attachments.name: image2.jpeg
attachments.visualDescription: A scan of page 8 of the book, two columns of text headed "The story begins", describing Brian Rankin's visit to the artist's family home on 4 February 2023. Below the text is a black and white photograph of Charlie Rogers as a younger man, seated on a stool in a light jacket and dark jumper, jars of brushes beside him and his own street paintings hung on the wall behind.

attachments.name: PBB Low Res.pdf
attachments.visualDescription: Not an image. The low resolution PDF of the book, named PBB Low Res.pdf, supplied so pages can be reproduced on the website. This is very probably the same source PDF referred to in the project docs as the low resolution book file.

attachments.name: Image-1.jpg
attachments.visualDescription: A colour photograph of a retail display, not artwork. Copies of the hardback "Charlie Rogers, Pursued by Bulldozers" stand in a wine red counter display box with a header card, on a table alongside other local interest titles including Forget Carter, Historic Tales From Newcastle and a High Cochrane title. A photocopier and printing and photocopying charges notices are visible behind, suggesting a library or community shop counter.

attachments.name: Image-1.jpg
attachments.visualDescription: A colour photograph, portrait format, of the book standing upright on a gravel path in a park with an avenue of cherry trees in full pink blossom arching overhead. The dust jacket shows the snowy back lane cover painting and the title "Pursued by Bulldozers, the life and times of a Gateshead artist". Almost certainly Saltwell Park.

attachments.name: Image-1.jpg
attachments.visualDescription: A colour photograph of the book propped on a speckled terrazzo ledge inside a glazed Victorian market hall with a barrel vaulted iron and glass roof, red and white striped stall canopies and shoppers below. The hall is the Grainger Market, Newcastle, with Pumphrey's Coffee Room visible on the right.

subject: The installation of the Charlie Rogers at Saltwell Towers exhibition at Saltwell Towers with Michael Timmins whose company Onesign and Digital designed and created the exhibition. February 2026
bodyText:
Photography courtesy of Darren Turner

Sent from my iPhone

mailDrop.label: Download full-resolution images
mailDrop.whatIsMissing: An Apple Mail Drop link to an iCloud archive named Images.zip, given in the message as 11,081,616 bytes. The link expired on 12 July 2026, so the full resolution versions of the installation photographs are unrecoverable from this email. Only the five embedded lower resolution copies listed below survive. Ask Brian Rankin to resend the originals if print or large format use is needed.

attachments.name: Image-1.jpg
attachments.visualDescription: A colour photograph, not a painting. A man in a black polo shirt and glasses stands outside the red brick and stone Saltwell Towers holding a large red bordered exhibition panel at chest height. The panel carries a black and white photograph of Charlie Rogers sketching at a cobbled kerb with the script title "Charlie Rogers at Saltwell Park".

attachments.name: image.png
attachments.visualDescription: A colour photograph of the exterior of Saltwell Towers, the Gothic revival red brick and banded stone mansion in Saltwell Park, seen from the approach path with clipped hedges, stone steps and a retaining wall under a flat grey sky. No people, no artwork.

attachments.name: image.png
attachments.visualDescription: An installation photograph. A grey haired man in glasses and a grey marl half zip top lifts a dark wood framed picture onto a wall hook. The frame holds a mounted sheet of handwritten manuscript with a small orange fragment at the left edge, not a painting.

attachments.name: image.png
attachments.visualDescription: An installation photograph. Two men carry a large canvas or framed work, back facing the camera with an inventory label on the stretcher, through a doorway in a modern interior with green panelling and a fire exit sign. The man in front wears a grey half zip top and glasses, the man behind a black polo with a small circular logo.

attachments.name: image.png
attachments.visualDescription: A colour photograph of a wine red cardboard counter display box filled with copies of the book, with the printed header card standing behind it showing the same snowy back lane cover painting and the title Pursued by Bulldozers. Shot against a stone sill and pale wall.

subject: Exhibition at Saltwell Towers
bodyText:
Michael Timmins and I celebrating the completion of the exhibition

Sent from my iPhone

mailDrop.label: Download full-resolution images
mailDrop.whatIsMissing: An Apple Mail Drop link to an iCloud archive named Images.zip, given in the message as 11,429,374 bytes. The link expired on 12 July 2026, so the full resolution versions of these completion photographs are unrecoverable from this email. Only the four embedded lower resolution copies listed below survive.

attachments.name: image.png
attachments.visualDescription: A colour photograph of a man, not a painting. A slim older man in a grey marl half zip top, holding his glasses, stands three quarter length in front of a large printed exhibition panel showing a loose watercolour of Saltwell Towers in pink, ochre and green with bare branches, plus three smaller inset images in a red border including a black and white studio portrait of Charlie Rogers.

attachments.name: image.png
attachments.visualDescription: A colour photograph of a smiling man in glasses and a black sweatshirt carrying a small oval "Come view my art" logo, standing to the right of the same Saltwell Towers exhibition panel. The watercolour of the Towers and the black and white studio portrait of Charlie Rogers are clearly legible on the panel, along with a small signed and dated 1988 sketch at top.

attachments.name: image.png
attachments.visualDescription: A close portrait photograph of the same slim older man in the grey marl half zip top, framed from the chest up, with the watercolour of Saltwell Towers filling the wall behind him. The tower, its slate spire and the trailing green branches are the dominant background.

attachments.name: Image-1.jpg
attachments.visualDescription: A colour photograph of both men standing either side of the finished red bordered exhibition panel in a bright room with a tall sash window. Per the email text this is Brian Rankin and Michael Timmins celebrating completion of the exhibition, though neither is individually labelled in the image.

subject: The book
bodyText:
Christopher Fairbank (who played Moxey in Auf Wiedersehen ) receives a signed copy of the book

Sent from my iPhone

attachments.name: Image-1.jpg
attachments.visualDescription: A colour photograph of a person, not a painting. An older bearded man in a fur trapper hat, wire glasses, a checked scarf and a blue quilted jacket stands on a pavement outside a lit shop front and a brown shuttered doorway, holding the book open faced to the camera. Per the email text this is the actor Christopher Fairbank receiving a signed copy.

attachments.name: Image-1.jpg
attachments.visualDescription: A close, shallow focus colour photograph of many copies of the book on a table at what looks like a launch or signing, two standing upright with the snowy back lane cover painting facing the camera and further copies stacked flat in front and behind. The artist's signature and the date 1980 are visible in the lower left of the cover painting.

subject: Charlie Rogers Talks are available to schools, art groups and other organisations
bodyText:
Charlie Rogers Talks personally presented by Brian Rankin
Ask for details

Sent from my iPhone

attachments.name: Image-1.jpg
attachments.visualDescription: A colour photograph of a talk in progress. A bald man in glasses and a black zip top speaks into a handheld microphone beside a gilt framed pencil sketch of several overlapping heads, displayed on a wooden easel. Behind him a roller banner headed PURSUED BY BULLDOZERS carries a sepia photograph of Charlie Rogers and small reproductions of his street scenes. Warm tungsten cast throughout.

attachments.name: image.png
attachments.visualDescription: A closer, tighter framing of the same talk. The speaker with the microphone fills the right of the frame, the gilt framed pencil sketch of overlapping faces the lower left, and the PURSUED BY BULLDOZERS roller banner with the large sepia portrait of Charlie Rogers fills the background. The speaker's polo carries a small "Come view my art" logo.

attachments.name: image.png
attachments.visualDescription: A portrait format colour photograph of the same speaker alone, from the waist up, microphone to his mouth against a plain warm lit wall. The "COME VIEW MY ART" chest logo is clearly readable. No artwork in shot.

attachments.name: Image-1.jpg
attachments.visualDescription: A colour photograph of the same bald, bearded man in glasses and a black polo, smiling behind a branded lectern reading "Newcastle Libraries, Turn a new page" with a laptop and notes on it. A large sepia Charlie Rogers roller banner stands behind to the right, a potted plant to the side.

subject: Images from the Charlie Rogers Summer Exhibition at Gateshead Central Library 12th July - 27th September 2025

attachments.name: Image-1.jpg
attachments.visualDescription: A colour photograph of a building exterior, not artwork. A classical stone library frontage with twin domed corner pavilions, a balustraded parapet, Ionic columns and the carved legend "A.D. PUBLIC LIBRARY 1926" above modern glass entrance doors. Blue sky, plane tree leaves in the foreground, a small feather flag by the steps. This is Gateshead Central Library.

attachments.name: image.png
attachments.visualDescription: A colour photograph of a man in a black polo with the "Come view my art" logo, glasses and a grey beard, signing the title page of an open copy of the book at a table. A striped photo album, a burgundy leaflet with a black and white photograph, and newspaper are on the table, framed Rogers works on the wall behind.

attachments.name: image.png
attachments.visualDescription: A colour photograph of the same man mid talk, hands raised, in a gallery hung with framed Rogers works and interpretation panels. A gold framed watercolour of a wet city street is captioned "Shipley Art Gallery, Dec..." and a black and white photograph below is captioned "Honorary Life Member Award, 1995". A video light on a stand is in shot at the right.

attachments.name: image.png
attachments.visualDescription: A colour photograph of two people laughing, not artwork. A white haired woman in a turquoise top leans over the shoulder of the seated bald bearded man in the black polo. Behind them a gallery wall headed "Newcastle" holds framed Rogers watercolours, a gold framed work and a framed newspaper cutting headed "Charlie finds his real knack", plus wall text mentioning reds and cool ochres.
